parameters.content:
## Monthly Reporting - Stock Template

Runs on the 1st of each month, for every active row in the Clients Registry (a new Google Sheet - see README), and compiles last calendar month's activity into a client-facing report emailed via Resend, plus an internal archive copy in Google Drive (one folder per client).

Reads data already produced by the existing systems rather than duplicating any of their logic:
- Phone Booking -> that client's CallLog sheet (new - see workflows/ai-phone-booking/03-post-call-actions.json) for calls answered / bookings made.
- Invoice Automation -> that client's Jobs sheet for invoices sent / cash jobs.
- Collections/Reminders -> Xero Invoice History (same tagged COLLECTIONS_STAGE entries Collections itself writes) for invoices chased / paid.
- Quoting -> not built yet; always skipped (usesQuoting is always false in the Registry today). Wired in now so nothing else needs to change when it exists.

A client with a service flag OFF in the Registry has that whole section omitted from their report entirely (not shown as zero/N/A). A client with a service ON but genuinely zero activity that month still gets that section, worded gracefully ("We didn't send any invoices this month.") rather than a bare 0.

Three triggers, same pattern as every other workflow in this project:
- Schedule Trigger: real production path, 1st of the month at 08:00.
- Manual Trigger + "Sample Mock Clients": click-to-test with 2 fictional trades businesses covering full-usage and partial-usage cases.
- Webhook (POST /webhook/reporting/monthly-check): accepts { testMode: true, mockClients: [...] } for API testing - this is what was used for the pre-live test run (see README).

testMode bypasses the real Clients Registry/Xero/Sheets fetch entirely (mock clients already carry their own fully-formed stats) but still sends a real Resend email and creates a real Drive archive file, so delivery is actually proven end to end, not just simulated.

See README.md for the Clients Registry sheet structure, the Drive folder setup, and flagged parameter-shape uncertainties - this workflow is the first in the project to call Google Drive at all, the first to use the Sheets values:append verb, and the first to make authenticated API calls from inside a Code node (this.helpers.httpRequestWithAuthentication) rather than a native node - all unverified until a live test proves them.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (1st of month 08:00)
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: the 'months'/triggerAtDayOfMonth field shape here is best-effort - only 'minutes' (Sheet Poller) and 'days'/triggerAtHour (Collections) have been proven live in this project so far. Verify the first scheduled run actually fires on the 1st.

const mockClients = [
  {
    clientId: 'MOCK-RIDGELINE',
    clientName: 'Ridgeline Plumbing & Heating',
    contactEmail: 'keystoneconsultancy.co@gmail.com',
    usesPhoneBooking: true,
    usesInvoiceAutomation: true,
    usesCollections: true,
    usesQuoting: false,
    callsAnswered: 47,
    bookingsMade: 22,
    quotesGiven: 0,
    invoicesSent: 19,
    invoicesChased: 5,
    invoicesPaid: 3,
    cashJobs: 6,
  },
  {
    clientId: 'MOCK-BRIGHTSPARK',
    clientName: 'Bright Spark Electrical',
    contactEmail: 'keystoneconsultancy.co@gmail.com',
    usesPhoneBooking: false,
    usesInvoiceAutomation: true,
    usesCollections: false,
    usesQuoting: false,
    callsAnswered: 0,
    bookingsMade: 0,
    quotesGiven: 0,
    invoicesSent: 0,
    invoicesChased: 0,
    invoicesPaid: 0,
    cashJobs: 0,
  },
];

return [{ json: { testMode: true, mockClients } }];

nodes.name: Sample Mock Clients (Manual Test)
nodes.notes: Two fixtures: Ridgeline uses every service with plausible mixed numbers (proves the normal case and graceful non-zero wording); Bright Spark uses only Invoice Automation with zero activity (proves both the 'skip unused service section entirely' rule AND the 'graceful zero wording for a used-but-quiet service' rule in one pass).

parameters.jsCode:
const body = $json.body || {};
return [{ json: { testMode: !!body.testMode, mockClients: Array.isArray(body.mockClients) ? body.mockClients : [] } }];

const input = $input.item.json;
const mockClients = input.mockClients || [];

return mockClients.map(c => ({ json: {
  clientId: c.clientId,
  clientName: c.clientName,
  contactEmail: c.contactEmail,
  usesPhoneBooking: !!c.usesPhoneBooking,
  usesInvoiceAutomation: !!c.usesInvoiceAutomation,
  usesCollections: !!c.usesCollections,
  usesQuoting: !!c.usesQuoting,
  callsAnswered: Number(c.callsAnswered) || 0,
  bookingsMade: Number(c.bookingsMade) || 0,
  quotesGiven: Number(c.quotesGiven) || 0,
  invoicesSent: Number(c.invoicesSent) || 0,
  invoicesChased: Number(c.invoicesChased) || 0,
  invoicesPaid: Number(c.invoicesPaid) || 0,
  cashJobs: Number(c.cashJobs) || 0,
  monthLabel: input.monthLabel,
  reportPeriodStart: input.reportPeriodStart,
  reportPeriodEnd: input.reportPeriodEnd,
  testMode: true,
  driveRootFolderId: input.driveRootFolderId,
  reportsFromEmail: input.reportsFromEmail,
} }));

nodes.name: Build Mock Clients
nodes.notes: Mock clients already carry their own fully-formed stats (no Sheets/Xero calls at all in test mode) - explodes the mockClients array into one item per client, same shape the real path produces, so both paths share the same downstream report-formatting/email/Drive logic.

nodes.name: Extract Tenant ID + Reporting Config
nodes.notes: Reporting Config values (reportingRegistrySheetId, driveRootFolderId, reportsFromEmail) are hardcoded here rather than pulled from a per-client Client Config sub-workflow, since this workflow serves ALL clients at once, not one - there's no single 'client' context to Execute Workflow against. Fill these in once, directly on the live deployment (same REPLACE_WITH_* convention as everywhere else).

nodes.name: Parse Active Clients
nodes.notes: Explodes the Clients Registry response into one item per ACTIVE client. jobsSheetId/reportingSheetId are read directly from the Registry (a synced copy of the values already in each client's own Invoice Automation / Phone Booking Client Config) rather than fetched live via Execute Workflow per client - see README for why (avoids two unproven n8n mechanisms: dynamic per-item sub-workflow IDs, and Execute Workflow's own per-item batch behavior, neither of which has been exercised anywhere in this project).

nodes.name: Compile Phone/Invoice Sheet Stats
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: this.helpers.httpRequestWithAuthentication('googleSheetsOAuth2Api', ...) called from inside a Code node - unlike every other Code-node HTTP call in this project (Sheet Poller, Collections), which called n8n's own unauthenticated webhook, this needs a REAL OAuth2-authenticated external call from within Code. Never done anywhere else in this project. Also requires this Code node to have a googleSheetsOAuth2Api credential attached (also new - Code nodes have never carried a credential before). Unverified until a live test proves both the credential-attachment and the helper method signature.

nodes.name: Compile Collections Stats
nodes.notes: Same this.helpers.httpRequestWithAuthentication uncertainty as the previous node, here with the xeroOAuth2Api credential type instead. One Xero call pair (Invoices by Reference + that invoice's History) per invoiced job last month - reuses the exact GET shapes already proven in 01-invoice-automation.json and 03-collections-reminders.json, just invoked from a Code node instead of a native httpRequest node.

nodes.name: Format Client Report
nodes.notes: Gating rule: a service flag OFF (usesPhoneBooking/usesInvoiceAutomation/usesCollections/usesQuoting) omits that whole section - never shown as zero. A service ON but genuinely zero this month still shows, worded gracefully ("We didn't send any invoices this month.") rather than a bare 0. cashJobs specifically is only mentioned when > 0 (a supplementary detail, not a headline metric) - the one deliberate exception to that rule, documented here since it's a judgement call.

nodes.name: Send Report Email (Resend)
nodes.notes: Resend API - POST /emails. Uses the 'Header Auth account 2' credential, same as every other Resend call in this project. reportsFromEmail is Keystone's own sending address (Reporting Config), not the client's confirmationFromEmail - this email is FROM Keystone TO the client, not the client's own outbound mail.

nodes.name: Mark Email Sent
nodes.notes: References $('Has Contact Email?') for the report data, not $input - by this point $input.item.json is the Resend API response, not the client/report fields (they'd otherwise be silently wiped).

nodes.name: Report Email Handled
nodes.notes: Convergence point for the email-sent/email-skipped branches, same purpose as 'Folder Resolved' below - lets 'Parse Folder Search Result' safely reference one guaranteed-to-have-run node (with emailSent already set) instead of 'Has Contact Email?' (which predates emailSent) or either branch-specific node directly (only one of which ran).

parameters.name: q
parameters.value: =name='{{ $json.clientName.replace(/'/g, "\\'") }}' and mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.folder' and trashed=false and '{{ $json.driveRootFolderId }}' in parents

nodes.name: Find Client Drive Folder
nodes.notes: Parameter-shape flag: first Google Drive API call anywhere in this project (only Calendar and Sheets have been used from Google so far). Needs a 'Google Drive OAuth2 API' credential in n8n - per the brief this should already exist alongside the Sheets/Calendar credentials, but that's unverified; if it doesn't exist, this needs the SAME underlying Google OAuth client granted Drive scope, or a separate Drive-scoped credential connecting the same Google account (still 'reusing existing auth', not a new provider).

nodes.name: Parse Folder Search Result
nodes.notes: References $('Has Contact Email?') for the base client/report data - that's the last node before the email/Drive fan-out that still carried the full item unchanged (both the email-sent and email-skipped branches passed through it without altering the fields this needs).

parameters.jsCode:
const resp = $input.item.json;
return { json: { ...$('Parse Folder Search Result').item.json, resolvedFolderId: resp.id } };

const d = $input.item.json;
return { json: { ...d, resolvedFolderId: d.existingFolderId } };

nodes.name: Folder Resolved
nodes.notes: Convergence point for the two folder-resolution branches (existing vs. just-created), same pattern as 'Contact Resolved' in 01-invoice-automation.json - lets downstream nodes safely reference $('Folder Resolved') regardless of which branch actually ran, instead of referencing one specific branch's node that might not have executed.

nodes.name: Create Report File (metadata)
nodes.notes: Two-step Drive upload (create metadata, then PATCH content below) rather than a single multipart/related upload call - n8n's httpRequest node doesn't have a built-in body type for Drive's specific multipart/related format, so this avoids hand-building that encoding.

nodes.name: Parse New File ID
nodes.notes: References $('Folder Resolved') - the shared convergence point - rather than either branch-specific node directly, since only one of those two ever actually runs per item.

nodes.name: Upload Report Content
nodes.notes: Raw-body upload confirmed live: the selector key is 'contentType: "raw"' (not 'specifyBody', which is only for the json/other body modes used elsewhere in this project) - 'rawContentType' + 'body' work as expected alongside it. Found via a live test after the first deploy silently uploaded a zero-byte file (no error, wrong parameter shape) - see README test results.
